_what: Numbers CLAUDE.md and the provenance docs ASSERT, each paired with an expression that measures the same thing from the live corpus. check_docs.py evaluates every expression and fails on any mismatch.
_why: Three documented numbers were stale or undefined on 2026-11-07 and none of them failed anything: the F-001 flag count (1,152, and the metric the docs told you to re-measure it with returned 1,652 -- F-024), the chance baseline (1/31 vitro, which matched neither the live corpus nor the frozen run -- F-026), and a trailing-space condition understated as 'several' when it was 915 cells (F-022). Prose cannot be audited. A number in prose with no executable twin drifts the moment the corpus moves, and the drift is invisible because nothing compares them.
_how: Add an entry whenever a doc states a number about the corpus. `expr` is evaluated with `V` (vitro rows), `W` (vivo rows), `O` (Original_LNPDB rows), `A` (audit_findings.json), `S` (schema_quality.json columns) in scope -- see check_docs.py. Keep `where` pointing at the file and section that makes the claim, so a failure says which prose to fix.  Each claim now carries `file`, and check_docs.py verifies that file exists before trusting the claim -- a claim pointing at a renamed or deleted doc would otherwise pass forever while documenting nothing. Added 2026-11-09 with the first claims outside CLAUDE.md: until then all 33 claims were tagged CLAUDE.md, so provenance/README.md sat four merges out of date (25,997 x 72, 40 experiments, 'Nine checks') and nothing could see it.
